'''Robert John Riggins''' (born August 4, 1949), nicknamed "'''Riggo'''" and "'''Diesel'''", is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[New York Jets]] and [[Washington Redskins]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas Jayhawks]]. Riggins was known for his "bell cow" running style and productivity well into the later years of his career. In the 1983 season, at age 34, he rushed for a then-NFL record of 24 touchdowns, a record which stood for almost 20 seasons. Riggins again led the league in rushing touchdowns during the 1984 season at age 35. Although he earned only one [[Pro Bowl]] appearance in his career, Riggins had his greatest success in the [[NFL playoffs|postseason]] and was named [[Super Bowl Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] of [[Super Bowl XVII]] where he scored one touchdown and rushed for 166 yards in a 27–17 win for the Redskins over the [[1982 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. Riggins was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 1992.

'''John Arnold Offerdahl''' (born August 17, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who spent his entire eight-year career as a [[linebacker]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Western Michigan Broncos football|Western Michigan Broncos]], before being selected by the Dolphins with the 52nd pick of the [[1986 NFL draft]].

While at WMU, Offerdahl set school records in tackles and recovered fumbles, making the All [[Mid-American Conference]] first-team his last three years, the Associated Press [[College Football All-America Team|All American]] third-team his junior year, and the All American second-team his senior year. In his professional career,  Offerdahl was selected for the [[Pro Bowl]] in each of his first five years in the league, and was a two-time [[All-Pro]]; in 1986 as a second-team selection and in 1990 as a first-team selection.

While still playing, Offerdahl opened a chain of bagel restaurants called Offerdahl's Bagel Gourmet, before selling the franchise in 1995. In 2000, he started a second franchise, Offerdahl's Cafe Grill.

'''Thomas Johnson''' "'''John'''" '''Reaves''' (March 2, 1950 – August 1, 2017) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] for 11 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and three seasons in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) during the 1970s and 1980s. '''John Anthony Rade''' (born August 31, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1983 to 1991 with the {{nowrap|[[Atlanta Falcons]].}}

Born in [[Ceres, California]], Rade graduated from [[Buena High School (Arizona)|Buena High School]] in [[Sierra Vista, Arizona]]. He attended [[Modesto Junior College]] and transferred to [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State University]] and played for the Broncos in [[1981 Boise State Broncos football team|1981]] and [[1982 Boise State Broncos football team|1982]]. He was an eighth-round draft choice in [[1983 NFL draft|1983]], 215th overall. In [[1988 Atlanta Falcons season|1988]], Rade led Atlanta in tackles with 137 for the second straight year. He had four 100-plus tackle seasons in six years. Rade played for the Atlanta Falcons from 1983 to [[1991 Atlanta Falcons season|1991]], posting a career high 145 tackles in [[1990 Atlanta Falcons season|1990]].

Rade served as assistant football coach and defensive coordinator at [[Wood River High School (Idaho)|Wood River High School]] in [[Hailey, Idaho]], with head football coach, Mike Glenn, before taking the job of athletic and activities director in 2007—first working for a year-and-a-half as assistant AD under athletic director Ron Martinez.

He is believed to be one of the longest-serving Wood River High athletic and activity directors, possibly the longest with nine full years on the director job. In 2009, Rade was named 4th District 5A/4A “Athletic Director of the Year.” He submitted his letter of resignation to principal John Pearce on Thursday, July 14. Rade's resignation was effective July 18.
